decisions.reason: As a technically adjacent extension of the wafer portfolio, it likely has modest carrying cost and still retains option value under uncertain demand, even without strong later signals.
This product is very close to the firm's core thin-wafer handling offer, so it is inexpensive to maintain and useful to keep available while customer demand across niches unfolds.

Because it was presented as a flagship technology in the firm's future direction and fits advanced wafer-level packaging capabilities, management would usually preserve this option unless failure were clearly revealed.

The off-the-shelf brand leverages existing glass and quartz know-how and broadens commercialization of standard products, so its strategic fit and relatively low uncertainty-resolution cost favor continuation.

Glass-based circuit boards are more distant from the firm's established substrate business and likely require greater ongoing commitment, so with several better-aligned options management would reallocate resources if traction remained unclear.
